**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the full text in embedding cache keys**

When two passages share their first 128 characters but differ afterward, they receive the same cache key. This aliases them even within a single `generate()` call, where the second passage reuses the first passage's in-flight embedding, and later cache hits continue returning that incorrect vector; long documents with common headers or boilerplate will therefore be indexed and ranked using another document's embedding. Hash the complete text rather than truncating it.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate failed per-entry embedding retries**

When a batch initially fails because one input exceeds the provider context, every entry is retried separately, but any subsequent error is converted to an empty vector here. A transient authentication, transport, or provider failure during an individual retry therefore makes `generate()` appear successful; graph indexing silently skips that row and scoped recall can remain `indexing-pending` indefinitely. Only continue splitting context-overflow failures and reject non-overflow retry errors.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use configured TTLs when writing expiring documents**

When an SDK consumer supplies `mongodb.eventsTtlSeconds` or `mongodb.compactedTtlSeconds` through the documented config override while the corresponding environment variable is unset, `openMongoDB` creates the TTL index from the override but vector writes compute `expiresAt` from the environment instead. Those documents receive no expiration date and bypass the configured retention policy; pass the resolved Mongo configuration into the write path rather than rereading process environment variables.
